description: This line plot illustrates how majority voting accuracy changes as the number of completions (k) increases, with two distinct curves representing different models or configurations. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k)”, uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from 2^0 to 2^5, with tick labels indicating powers of two and the axis values increasing by one power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Majority voting accuracy”, is linear and ranges from 0.3 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The upper curve, depicted with solid blue lines and filled blue triangles, starts at approximately 0.43 when k=2^0 and rises steadily to about 0.61 at k=2^5, showing a consistent increase in accuracy. The lower curve, shown with dashed light blue lines and filled light blue diamonds, begins near 0.27 at k=2^0 and increases more gradually to approximately 0.43 at k=2^5, remaining consistently below the upper curve throughout the range.
